prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper): intake/triage/authorized-dispatch; preserves reports/clarifications, records selection reason/authorization-time/conditions, escalates gaps, maintains location/crew/readiness-based coverage; produces Unit Staging Change Card. Jurisdictions retain ownership/policy. Shift Commander (Sundial): continuity/surge/readiness; receives capacity-exceedance alerts, reviews coverage before staging approval, approves coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions, escalates beyond-authority; cannot override clinical authority/crew judgment. Regional Medical Director: clinical policy/delegation/escalation, unusual-resource advice, not dispatch. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): verifies location first, captures callback/symptoms/onset/hazards/access, separates observed/reported; produces Caller Location Correction Slip; updates before dispatch, follows unresolved locations. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): clarifies/reassesses deterioration/disagreements without delaying urgency, documents priority rationale/response consistency, escalates clinically; sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Immediate threats: highest-available-priority/prompt-dispatch. Computer Aided Dispatch Console: current authorized details/priority/travel/availability/access and demand/travel/access-based staging options; verify currency. Ambulance Coordination Platform: consolidates positions/status; compares coverage, matches priority/capability/availability/constraints. Selection requires regional authorization and confirmed priority/essential requirements; weighs clinical-need/travel/capability/readiness/coverage. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): manages Regional Radio Network/reachability/backups/faults; selects/confirms available talkgroup. Transmission: incident-identifier/location/priority/assignment/hazards; dispatcher explicitly identifies confirmed gate/approach constraints/uncertainty, corrects discrepancies by fresh transmission. Paramedic Crew acknowledges/repeats location/priority; controlled handoff requires acknowledgment and dispatch-floor confirmation. Missing prompt acknowledgment: retry/alert dispatch supervisor. Sends Coverage Gap Bulletin below regional coverage threshold. Network carries routes/acknowledgments; Mistral confirms approved changes before diversion. Paramedic Crew: scope/protocol treatment; reports condition/access/route-conflicts/status promptly: available/responding/on-scene/transporting/temporarily-unavailable; remains staged until confirmed relocation/direct-response. Ambulance Unit 417 follows instructions/requests safety clarification; reports staging-entry/exit position/status. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): reports unavailability/restrictions, produces Battery Swap Voucher, verifies return-to-available clearance. Hospital Liaison Desk

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
